item.title: Decode One Instruction — 2026-09-09 (Windows x86-64)
item.description:
Challenge: Decode this instruction (Intel syntax), byte by byte:
48 89 04 24
Give the mnemonic and full operands.
Answer: mov qword ptr [rsp], rax -- 48 is REX.W, forcing 64-bit operand size; 89 is MOV r/m64, r64, so a register goes into a memory operand or another register. ModRM 04 = 00 000 100: mod=00 (no displacement), reg=000 (RAX, the source), rm=100 -- this rm value doesn't name RSP directly, it's the escape code meaning "a SIB byte follows." SIB 24 = 00 100 100: scale bits are unused, index=100 (the "no index" sentinel), base=100 (RSP). RSP can only appear as a memory base through this SIB detour, never via a bare ModRM rm field, so the final address is just [rsp] with rax stored into it.
